questions.q: How do you reach the Data Flow tab in SSIS Designer?
options: Through a Data Flow task on the Control Flow surface
Through the File menu's "New Data Flow" command
It is always visible regardless of what's on Control Flow
By right-clicking Solution Explorer and choosing Add Data Flow
questions.explain: A Data Flow task is a wrapper on the control flow; double-clicking it (or selecting it and clicking the Data Flow tab) opens its own design surface.

questions.q: What are the three kinds of data flow components?
options: Sources, transformations, and destinations
Tasks, containers, and precedence constraints
Connection managers, variables, and parameters
Buffers, rows, and columns
questions.explain: Sources extract data, transformations modify it in place, and destinations write it out — connected by paths.

questions.q: Which data flow component type has ONLY an input, with no regular output back into the data flow?
options: Destinations
Sources
Transformations
Connection managers
questions.explain: Destinations write rows out of the data flow into a data store; nothing flows from them back into the pipeline except an optional error output.

questions.q: What does a component's error output carry?
options: Rows that failed, plus ErrorCode and ErrorColumn columns describing what went wrong
A log of every successful row that passed through
The SQL text used to configure the component
A backup copy of the entire data flow for recovery
questions.explain: An error output contains the same columns as the regular output plus ErrorCode and ErrorColumn, so you can redirect and inspect failed rows separately.

questions.q: Is a data flow required to include any transformations?
options: No — a source connected directly to a destination is a valid data flow
Yes — every data flow must include at least one transformation
Only if the source is a flat file
Only if the destination has an error output
questions.explain: Transformations are optional. Many real data flows are nothing more than a source piped straight into a destination.
